root_cause_criterion.missing_conjunct: The `test` object materialized by `StripString(input, "\t\r\n ", &r.pos)` preserves at least the initialized prefix already present in `input` before `test.size()` consumes it.
root_cause_criterion.criterion: At the `StripString` store site, the initialized prefix of the new `test` object must be no smaller than the initialized prefix already present in the source `input` object on the same path.
root_cause_criterion.description: The vulnerable run reaches line 82 with `input_initialized_prefix_len=3` but materializes `test` with `test_initialized_prefix_len=0`, so the substring copy degrades already-initialized string state before the sink. The fixed image reaches the same line with `input_initialized_prefix_len=3` and `test_initialized_prefix_len=3`, preserving that prefix and making the required assertion genuine.

nodes.state: At `r.len = test.size();`, the `test` object queried by `size()` still contains an uninitialized tail in its `std::string` object state on the vulnerable execution.
At `auto input = std::string(original.c_str());`, the new `input` object already has only a 3-byte initialized prefix within its 24-byte `std::string` object state.

edges.relation: The partially initialized `input` object created at line 246 reaches `StripString(input, ...)`, where the vulnerable substring copy degrades the initialized prefix from 3 bytes to 0 before publishing the new `test` object.
The same `test` object materialized by `StripString` is immediately queried by `test.size()`, carrying the partially initialized `std::string` state into the sink.
